findings.text: MUST-FIX. The aperture can still shrink silently, and the surviving bypass is CHEAPER than the one this node closed. After the repair nothing in the tree states WHICH surfaces must be guarded - REQUIRED_MODULE_ROOTS was the only such statement and it was deleted rather than repaired - so the file's whole protection of root membership is two aggregate floors over totals. A pure deletion is genuinely refused (I reproduced it: exit 1, 'AssertionError: scanned 10 modules, below the ratchet floor of 11'). A SUBSTITUTION is not. TRIGGERING INPUT, one line, measured not argued: change line 16 from Path("imas_codex/standard_names/export.py") to Path("imas_codex/standard_names/fanout/runners.py"). That module contributes 1 module and 13 literal three-argument candidates with 0 violations, so the scan measures 11 modules and 40 candidates against floors of 11 and 30, and the focused file returns exit 0, 4 passed, 3 warnings in 30.41s. imas_codex/standard_names/export.py is then no longer guarded at all and no test says a word. The previous bypass cost two lines (delete a root from both lists); this one costs one. Per-root counts that make substitutions easy to find: review/ 9 modules 18 candidates, export.py 1/3, loop.py 1/9 - and 14 modules elsewhere in imas_codex carry >=3 literal candidates with zero violations, so a violation-free substitute is abundant. The first substitute I tried, audits.py, failed - but on test_defaulted_literal_attributes_are_declared because audits.py has real violations, NOT on the aperture test, which passed. The aperture guard did not object to the swap in either attempt. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: assert membership against something the guard does not itself author - e.g. require that every module under imas_codex/standard_names/ carrying a literal three-argument getattr is reachable from some configured root, which is derived from the tree rather than copied from the configuration, and which no substitution satisfies.

MUST-FIX (dead guard). `assert root.exists, f"configured module root is missing: {root.root}"` can no longer fail. _python_modules now raises for any path that is neither a directory nor a regular file, and it is called at line 134 BEFORE the ModuleRootScan carrying `exists` is constructed at line 156, so every root that reaches the assertion has exists()==True by construction. TRIGGERING INPUT: any root at all - the assertion is unreachable-false for every possible MODULE_ROOTS. I verified the raise fires for all three ways a path can fail the dir/file test: an absent path, a FIFO (exists() True, is_dir False, is_file False - raises), and a broken symlink (raises). So the `exists` field of ModuleRootScan and its assertion now report a protection that cannot be exercised, which is the same defect shape this plan closed elsewhere: a guard that never runs. Either delete the field and the assertion, or keep `exists` and stop raising - not both. This is a new dead guard introduced BY this change, not a pre-existing one.

SHOULD-FIX (test aperture). test_misspelled_module_root_raises drives only the ABSENT-path case. The docstring and the production message both say 'neither a directory nor a file', which is a strictly wider condition, and the wider half is untested. I verified out of tree that a FIFO at imas_codex/standard_names/pipe.py raises FileNotFoundError naming the resolved path, and so does a broken symlink - so the behaviour is correct today and the missing work is one parametrised case, not a repair. The existing test IS load-bearing for the branch it covers: under the declared revert (replace the raise with `return []`) the focused file returns exit 1, '1 failed, 3 passed', failing exactly on test_misspelled_module_root_raises with 'Failed: DID NOT RAISE <class \'FileNotFoundError\'>' - log at log-probe-revert-raise-red.log.

SHOULD-FIX, and out of this node's declared scope - reported here because fence question FOUR asks it, and the worker disclosed both instances in its own follow_ons rather than concealing them. The retirement the node DID own is clean: the archive file now contains 0 occurrences of MINIMUM_DECLARED_CLASS_ATTRIBUTES, declared_attribute_count, '3,000 declared class attributes' or '4,013', and grep over imas_codex/ and tests/ returns no REQUIRED_MODULE_ROOTS. Two orphans survive, both outside the four items. ONE, this archive's section #defaulted-attribute-guard-controls, paragraph 'Root contract': 'The test retains both the configured tuple and an independent required-root set', and it quotes a failure string 'required module roots are missing: imas_codex/standard_names/export.py' that the code can no longer emit because the symbol producing it is deleted. TWO, docs/plans/sn-lifecycle-integrity.html:731 still states 'at least 8 scanned modules, 3,000 declared class attributes and 24 literal three-argument calls' - two superseded floors plus one deleted floor. (The same file's line 922 also names REQUIRED_MODULE_ROOTS but is a review record of a past state, so it is correctly historical, not an orphan.) Structure of what the node did write is sound: 17 <section> opens against 17 closes, the new anchor #static-check-aperture-cannot-shrink-silently exists and the retirement paragraph's link to it resolves within the file.

justifications.durability: The weakest dimension, and the reason for the verdict. Three compounding issues. ONE, the ratchet protects a quantity while the thing at risk is a membership, so it is bypassed by any edit that keeps the quantity up - measured, one line, still green. TWO, a floor pinned to the measured value does not maintain itself in either direction. Upward: growth passes silently and converts into slack that a later shrink can spend - my single substitution moved the candidate count to 40 against a floor of 30, creating 10 candidates of silent-shrink headroom in one edit, with nothing to force the floor up afterwards. Downward: a LEGITIMATE deletion (retiring a dead module) turns the file red, and the only mechanical remedy is to lower the floor, which the assertion message explicitly forbids in the same breath - 'never lower it to make a failure go away'. The guard therefore has no sanctioned path for its most ordinary legitimate future, so the first real shrink puts the next engineer in conflict with the instruction and the likely outcome is the edit the message was written to prevent. A ratchet needs a stated procedure for the authorised ratchet-down, not a prohibition. THREE, the change introduces a dead assertion (root.exists is now unreachable-false), which is the failure mode this plan exists to remove. 12.
justifications.evidence: Strong, and it survives independent re-measurement. I re-ran everything load-bearing in a scratch mirror outside the repository (symlinked imas_codex, copied conftests and pyproject) whose unmutated control is 4 passed at exit 0. The base bypass claim reproduces. The declared negative control reproduces with the exact message the manifest quotes. The floors are the true measured values, not transcriptions: an independent scan of the integrated head returns module_count 11, candidate_count 30, violations 0, with per-root breakdown review/ 9/18, export.py 1/3, loop.py 1/9 - equal to the floors on the nose. Deductions: the new raise is tested for one of the two conditions its own message states; nothing pins the now-dead exists field; and no evidence was taken for the substitution case, which is the case that matters. One instrument caveat I hit and record so the next reader does not misread it: pytest-timeout's 30s default fires DURING failure-repr rendering on this file and returns INTERNALERROR at exit 3, which looks like a reproduction and proves nothing - every red result quoted here was re-taken with --timeout=300 and is exit 1. 17.
justifications.fit: Idiomatic for the repository and for this plan's house style: mechanism-first docstrings, assertion messages that state the rule rather than the incident, a commit body that explains the defect before the repair, an archived record that retires the false sentence in place with a stated reason for not renumbering it, and a figure carrying an aria-label that reads as prose. The retirement paragraph links forward to the new section and the anchor resolves. Minor: the assertion messages are four lines of prose each and repeat the same sentence twice, which pushes policy into an assertion string where a module-level comment would carry it once; and the new archive anchor is spelled from the node id, though that matches the two sibling sections already in the file. 16.
justifications.goal_fidelity: All four declared spec items are delivered and I verified each from the landed diff rather than the report: the duplicate list and its assertion are gone, the floors read 11 and 30, the non-dir/non-file branch raises, and the stale archived figures are retired. What is NOT delivered is the property the node is named for. The aperture CAN still shrink silently, one line, proved green at exit 0. Answering the fence directly - is the third iteration different in kind or merely harder to bypass? PARTLY DIFFERENT IN KIND, and that part is real: the first version's floors were unanchored constants, the second anchored root membership to a copy of itself (a control that is a copy of its subject cannot see the subject move), and the third anchors the floors to a MEASUREMENT OF THE TREE. That is a genuine change of reference - an external fact rather than a self-reference - and it is why removal-without-replacement is now refused on a count. But the change also narrowed the claim: the guard now asserts 'the totals did not fall', and 'these specific surfaces are guarded' has no assertion anywhere in the repository. On the node's own axis it is therefore not harder to bypass at all - the bypass got one line cheaper. 15.
justifications.scope_discipline: Exemplary. Exactly the three declared paths, no more; the diff is 38 insertions and 21 deletions in the test file plus two documentation edits. The worker found two further stale-prose sites - an adjacent archived section and a plan comment - both squarely in files it already had open and both one edit away, and it left them alone and reported them under follow_ons. It also explicitly retained the per-root coverage assertion instead of tidying it away, with a stated reason. No plan labels or ticket identifiers in the code or the commit subjects, no AI attribution, conventional subject with a mechanism body on both commits. 19.

raw_text:
FOUR ANSWERS, EACH MEASURED FROM THE LANDED DIFF AT THE INTEGRATED HEAD (bab2ed2404a32d31dd70c833ebcf26ef175586ba; both reviewed commits 5d5ac0dae and f44fceae9 are ancestors of it, checked with git merge-base --is-ancestor).

INSTRUMENT. Everything below was re-run in a scratch mirror at /dev/shm/mcintos-aperture-probe - a real tests/ tree with imas_codex symlinked to the worktree and pyproject/conftests copied - so no file in the assigned worktree was touched. The mirror's unmutated control is 4 passed, exit 0 (log-scratch-control-green.log), which is the positive control that the instrument can see the guard working before any absence is reported. Caveat worth carrying forward: pytest-timeout's 30s default fires while rendering the failure repr for this file and yields INTERNALERROR at exit 3, which reads like a reproduction and is not one; every red below was re-taken with --timeout=300 and is exit 1, a real test failure.

ONE - CAN THE APERTURE STILL SHRINK WITHOUT A TEST FAILING? YES, and the surviving edit is one line, cheaper than the two-line bypass this node closed.
  Pure removal is now genuinely refused. Deleting Path("imas_codex/standard_names/export.py") from MODULE_ROOTS gives exit 1, '1 failed, 3 passed', on 'AssertionError: scanned 10 modules, below the ratchet floor of 11' (log-probe-pure-removal-red.log). That is a real change from the predecessor and it is what the module floor buys.
  Substitution is not refused. Changing that same line to Path("imas_codex/standard_names/fanout/runners.py") gives exit 0, '4 passed, 3 warnings in 30.41s' (log-probe-substitution-green.log). export.py is then outside the guarded surface entirely and nothing reports it. The scan measures 11 modules and 40 candidates against floors of 11 and 30.
  WHAT NOW BLOCKS A SHRINK, precisely: only the two aggregate totals. WHAT DOES NOT: nothing at all states which roots must be present. REQUIRED_MODULE_ROOTS was the only statement of that property and it was deleted rather than repaired. Substitutes are easy to find - 14 modules under imas_codex/ carry >=3 literal three-argument getattr calls with zero violations. My first attempt, audits.py, did fail, but on test_defaulted_literal_attributes_are_declared because audits.py contains real violations; test_configured_module_roots_have_coverage PASSED under that swap too. The aperture test has not objected to either substitution I put to it.
  IS THE THIRD ITERATION DIFFERENT IN KIND? Partly, and honestly so. The anchor moved from self-reference to an external measurement of the tree, and that is a real change - a control that is a copy of its subject cannot see its subject move, and this one is not. But the claim was narrowed at the same time, from 'these surfaces are guarded' to 'the totals did not fall', and only the second is now asserted. On the axis the node is named for, it is not harder to bypass; it is one line easier.

TWO - ARE 11 AND 30 TRUE, AND WHAT HAPPENS WHEN THE TREE GROWS?
  True, independently measured, not transcribed. An independent scan at the integrated head returns module_count 11, candidate_count 30, violations 0; per root: imas_codex/standard_names/review 9 modules / 18 candidates, export.py 1/3, loop.py 1/9. 9+1+1 = 11 and 18+3+9 = 30. The floors equal the measurement exactly.
  ON GROWTH, BOTH DIRECTIONS FAIL TO MAINTAIN THEMSELVES. Upward: the comparison is >=, so growth passes silently and immediately becomes slack a later shrink can spend, with nothing forcing the floor up. This is not hypothetical - my one-line substitution took the candidate count to 40 against a floor of 30, minting 10 candidates of silent-shrink headroom in a single edit. Downward: a legitimate deletion (retiring a dead module) turns the file red, and the only mechanical remedy available is to lower the floor - which the assertion message forbids in the same sentence, 'never lower it to make a failure go away'. So the guard has no sanctioned procedure for its most ordinary legitimate future, and the first real shrink puts an engineer in direct conflict with the instruction. A ratchet needs a documented authorised ratchet-down (state the reason beside the new value), not a prohibition on the only move available.

THREE - DOES THE MISSPELLED-ROOT CASE RAISE, FOR BOTH CONDITIONS, AND IS THE TEST LOAD-BEARING?
  It raises for an ABSENT path: 'configured module root is neither a directory nor a file: <root>/imas_codex/standard_names/reviwe'.
  It raises for a path that EXISTS but is neither a directory nor a regular file: a FIFO at imas_codex/standard_names/pipe.py has exists() True, is_dir False, is_file False, and raises FileNotFoundError naming the resolved path. A broken symlink raises too. So the production behaviour covers both halves of its own message.
  The new test IS load-bearing, for the half it covers. Reverting the raise to `return []` gives exit 1, '1 failed, 3 passed', failing exactly on test_misspelled_module_root_raises with 'Failed: DID NOT RAISE <class FileNotFoundError>' (log-probe-revert-raise-red.log, whose first line names the mutation).
  But the test drives only the absent case, so the exists-but-not-a-regular-file half is correct and unpinned. And the raise made an older assertion dead: root.exists at line 193 can no longer be False, because _python_modules raises at line 134 before the ModuleRootScan carrying that flag is built at line 156.

FOUR - DID THE RETIREMENT LEAVE AN ORPHANED CROSS-REFERENCE? YES, TWO - both already disclosed by the worker, both outside the four items it was scoped to close.
  What the node owned is clean: the archive file now has 0 occurrences of MINIMUM_DECLARED_CLASS_ATTRIBUTES, declared_attribute_count, '3,000 declared class attributes' and '4,013'; REQUIRED_MODULE_ROOTS appears nowhere under imas_codex/ or tests/; 17 section opens against 17 closes; the new anchor #static-check-aperture-cannot-shrink-silently exists and the retirement paragraph's link to it resolves.
  Orphan one, docs/evidence/archive/sn-lifecycle-integrity-landed.html:1318, section #defaulted-attribute-guard-controls: 'The test retains both the configured tuple and an independent required-root set', quoting a failure string 'required module roots are missing: ...' the code can no longer emit.
  Orphan two, docs/plans/sn-lifecycle-integrity.html:731: 'at least 8 scanned modules, 3,000 declared class attributes and 24 literal three-argument calls' - two superseded floors and one deleted floor. Line 922 of the same file also names REQUIRED_MODULE_ROOTS but is a review record of a past state and is correctly historical.

VERDICT MUST-FIX. Two must-fix findings, both in this node's own change and both proved by running them rather than by reading: the substitution bypass (one line, green at exit 0) and the newly dead root.exists assertion. The four declared items were delivered faithfully and the evidence behind them survives independent re-measurement; the node's named property does not hold.
